newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AIR CHARTER SERVICE NAMED GSA FOR ESPACE AVIATION.
newsitem.headline: AIR CHARTER SERVICE NAMED GSA FOR ESPACE AVIATION.

text.p: Air Charter Service (ACS) said it has been appointed European general sales agent for a new charter airline, Espace Aviation Service.
Espace Aviation Service is headquartered in Zaire and has a branch in Beirut. The company will operate a 40 tonne Boeing 707 freighter from Ostend.
Jean-Paul De Zutter, general manager for the Ostend-based ACS, said he hopes to have at least 150 hours of flying time from the aircraft during the peak autumn months.
The aircraft was converted into a freighter in Beirut from a former MEA passenger Boeing 707-347C, he added.

Espace Aviation Service has acquired two other 707 aircraft from MEA, one of which has already been converted into a freighter, said De Zutter. This aircraft is expected at the end of September but although not necessarily out of Ostend, he added.
It has not yet been decided where the other two will operate, but it is likely that one will fly internally in Africa, De Zutter said.
Espace Aviation Service has been in the aviation industry for some time but this is its first venture as an airline operator. The company was previously chartering space to Kinshasa, said De Zutter.
In September, the airline will start to fly to Beijing once a month from Ostend and it hopes to start flying cattle from Ostend to Beirut and return via Cairo with beans as cargo, he added.
There have been many enquiries for destinations in the Middle East and Africa, but competition is tough with many very low rates on offer, he added.
Espace Aviation Service also has a noise exemption at Ostend airport so it can operate until the year 2002, De Zutter said.
If carriers do not have this European Union exemption they have to leave Ostend by end-1997 as part of EU moves to disocurage noisier, older aircraft such as the Douglas DC-8 and 707.
